---
title: "Pairwise errors from joint posterior draws"
subtitle: "4.11 · after postrank’s posterior-input vignettes"
description: "Pairing values from different posterior draws can change the estimated direction errors."
---

Each draw records all units and criteria in one joint state. Shifting one unit's rows keeps its marginal values while changing its pairwise comparisons.

```{=html}
<div id="app" class="prx-app column-page"></div>

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Original states** and **Full cycle.** Across 32 states, `001` above `site-B` is wrong 8 times (.250) on `need_A` and 32 times (1.00) on `need_B`.
- **Shift one unit** and **Move states together.** Shifting `site-B` gives 7 times (.219) on `need_A`; shifting all units restores 8 times and 32 times.
- **Short prefix** and **Unshifted pair.** At 8 retained states a shared shift alters the prefix; pair `001 / site C` keeps 0 times and 25 times (.781).

<details>
<summary>Sampling and dependence notes</summary>

The original states are independent draws from the same synthetic normal law. An empirical share of zero means that no retained draw realized the event; its underlying posterior probability can still be positive. Cyclic shifts reuse the same 32 vectors to isolate how cross-unit pairing affects pairwise error estimates.
</details>

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
e <- postrank_pairwise(postrank_toy)$e
e["001", "site-B", ]  # need_A .25, need_B 1
```
:::
